thread:
sara: Hey folks — heads up I'm planning to work from Toronto for ~10 weeks starting May 6 to support a client on-site. Would that trigger any tax nexus / payroll changes? Also wondering if WFH stipend still applies for that period.

maria (People Ops): @sara thanks for flagging! A few quick Qs: will you remain on Redwood payroll and be working for Redwood full-time while there? Any client invoice/contract that might create a local PE? :thinking_face:

sara: Yes, still on Redwood payroll, full-time, just co-located with client. No transfer of contract, just on-site collaboration. My partner might be with me for 3 weeks but not working.

chris (Payroll): @sara @maria short answer: possibly. Canada has provincial residency and withholding rules. 10 weeks is borderline but could create provincial reporting depending on activities. We need exact dates + confirmation there's no local payroll being paid by the client.

emma (Legal): Also confirm whether you'll be furnishing any services directly invoiced by the client or signing any SOWs in Canada. That can change the assessment for a permanent establishment. If not, lower risk but still will run it by counsel.

jen (Manager): +1 — team supports this. Please submit the formal remote-work request so People Ops has it on file. If there's any extra paperwork for the client site let me know. :thumbsup:

maria (People Ops): Action items for @sara: 1) Fill the short remote-location form: https://go.redwoodinference.com/remote-request  (select "temporary > 30 days") 2) Reply here with exact dates and city/province 3) Confirm you won't be on the client's payroll or signing local SOWs. We'll kick off payroll/legal review.

sara: Form submitted (link in form confirmation email). Dates: 2026-05-06 to 2026-07-15. City: Toronto, ON. Not joining client payroll, no local SOWs.

chris (Payroll): Got it. We'll queue a Canada payroll nexus checklist. Likely items: tax withholding check, benefits eligibility note, potential CPP/QPP/CPP equivalency, and whether insurance/coverage needs updates. Expect a follow-up in 3-4 business days.

maria (People Ops): Regarding WFH stipend: Our policy covers home office stipend for primary work location. For temporary travel >30 days we typically pause recurring WFH stipends and offer a short-term travel reimbursement for workspace (co-working or hotel workspace) up to policy limits. @sara we'll confirm exact amounts after nexus review.

emma (Legal): I ran a quick check with counsel — 10 weeks usually doesn't create a Canadian corporate PE for advisory-only onsite work, but each case is fact-dependent. We'll do the formal memo. Please don't sign any new client documents in-country until cleared.

chris (Payroll): Also: equipment shipping — if you need your laptop shipped to Canada, let us know. Shipping and temporary import documentation may be needed. If you keep company equipment with you, tag it in the asset system: "temp-toronto-2026".

hr-bot: Reminder: submit travel authorization in Triply (travel.redwood) if any client in-person security checks are required.

maria (People Ops): Expected timeline: payroll/legal review and final guidance by EOD Friday (2026-03-27). If any issues, we'll coordinate options (shorten trip, local contractor setup, or shadowing schedule adjustments).

sara: Awesome, thanks everyone. Appreciate the quick triage. Will wait for the confirmation before finalizing flights. :airplane: 

jen (Manager): Thanks @sara — ping me if the dates shift. If payroll/legal need anything from me, happy to provide client context.

maria (People Ops): Noted — marking as "under review". We'll post the update in this thread when complete. :white_check_mark:
